body:
## Summary

- accept exact model IDs discovered from the installed Codex CLI or the merged router/provider catalogue instead of limiting execution to release-time aliases
- default Codex to the newest numeric `gpt-*-sol` exposed by the installed CLI, with `gpt-6-sol` as the bundled offline default
- preserve Claude Code's rolling `opus` alias for direct execution and resolve it to the newest concrete Opus ID for routed execution
- apply the same runtime-aware behavior to solve, hive, task, organizer, connection checks, agent-commander, and Telegram solve/hive/fix/task paths
- add current GPT-6 Sol/Luna/Reserve and Claude Opus 5.5 catalogue metadata, a changeset, multilingual docs, and a full evidence-backed case study

## Root cause

PR #2203 made live model discovery available to `/models`, but command validation still used only the bundled model map. Hive Mind could therefore display a newly released model and reject that same exact ID before the provider was invoked. Claude's rolling `opus` alias was also eagerly converted to a concrete release, defeating the vendor-managed default.

The fix keeps bundled aliases and typo suggestions as the first layer, then accepts only exact IDs reported by an authoritative runtime catalogue. Codex deliberately does not use a broad `gpt-*` regex, so `gpt-6-slo` still fails closed with a `gpt-6-sol` suggestion.

## Reproduction

Before this change, the following Telegram command was rejected locally even though `codex debug models` advertised `gpt-6-sol`:

```text
/codex <issue> --model gpt-6-sol --think xhigh --auto-merge
```

![Telegram rejecting GPT-6 Sol before the fix](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2290-9da101d37b7c/docs/case-studies/issue-2290/evidence/issue-screenshot.png?raw=true)

The regression test now proves current Sol/Opus behavior, direct and routed resolution, a hypothetical future `gpt-6.1-sol`, exact live-only IDs, and typo rejection.

## Verification

- `npm test` — all 502 selected test files passed
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `npm run check:secrets`
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `node tests/docs-validation.mjs`
- `node tests/test-docs-language-sync.mjs`
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` with the PR base/head SHAs
- `node scripts/check-version.mjs`

## Investigation record

The [issue #2290 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2290-9da101d37b7c/docs/case-studies/issue-2290/README.md) contains the evidence hashes, runtime catalogue, timeline, requirements, causal trace, alternatives, dependency analysis, security constraints, and verification matrix. No upstream issue was opened because the router and vendor CLIs already expose the required catalogue/alias behavior; the broken boundary was local to Hive Mind.

Fixes #2290
title: Support live model IDs and default to latest Opus and GPT Sol
